Scope: infrastructure over about 6.5 km² of the Fourth Industrial City in Riyadh: roads and tunnels, electrical, telecom, ICT and security networks, potable water and fire-fighting, irrigation, sewage and stormwater networks, and sewage and stormwater pumping stations.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At 30.0% against 32.2% planned, the project is behind by 2.1% (SPI 0.93). It gained 1.5% this week against 0.6% planned, so the gap narrowed from 3.0% last week. More than half of this week's gain again came from procurement (1,980 of 3,594 earned man-hours), followed by the tunnels (739). Earthworks remain far ahead of plan, but procurement, the zone network works and the tunnels are still behind, and Zones 1, 2 and 9 earned no man-hours this week.

The schedule still finishes the project about eight months late. The P6 update uploaded this week (data date 16-Nov-2026) finishes the project on 14-Jan-2029, 229 days after the contract completion date of 30-May-2028 (last week: 17-Jan-2029, −232 days). The weekly report gives the same date. In P6 the roads finish on 25-Apr-2027 and the MV network on 31-Oct-2027, against the contract milestone of 30-Sep-2026 for MV and road works.

Clash with Green Riyadh servicesContractor / Green RiyadhAn air vent and cathodic protection on Road C8 clash with the works. Coordination with Green Riyadh's contractor is ongoing to get drawings and price the diversion. Rated critical; target moved again, to 30-Nov-2026.

Progress behind planContractorProgress lags the schedule because of the master plan change (Wadi Al-Sulai) and the equipment shortage at the start. Equipment and network crews were increased; the presentation targets 30-Nov-2026. Rated critical.
SEC cable clashes (closed)Contractor / SECBoth clashes are now closed. On Road C2 the contractor appointed by SEC has started and is supporting the high-voltage cables. On Road C8 a start-of-work record was signed with SEC's contractor (Pillar).

Delay reasons stated in the report: the master layout changed after the Wadi Al-Sulai redesign, which changed the design of all networks; and equipment was short at the start of the project.

Data notes

This report uses the files uploaded for 16-Nov-2026 (weekly report, progress presentation, quantities and procurement file, P6 update, MASTER LOG, material tracking sheet and the invoice 10 backup) and, for this-week values, the 09-Nov-2026 report. Every progress percentage is physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. There is no S-curve section: the workbook's Physical-Chart Data sheet is empty.

  • The week number, 50, is the contract week stated on the Milestones sheet ("Current Contract Weeks: 50 of 130"); it also equals the whole weeks from site handover (30-Nov-2025) to the data date (351 days).
  • The workbook and the presentation also give a cost-based progress figure, labelled as actual progress in places. This report does not use it.
  • The forecast finish agrees between the P6 update, the P6 extract in the lower table of the Progress sheet and the General Information sheet (14-Jan-2029, −229 days), but the upper table of the Progress sheet again carries last week's values (17-Jan-2029, −232 days). The Milestones sheet still shows no delay on any milestone.
  • Mobilisation finished on 29-Dec-2025 according to P6 and the presentation, but on 30-Mar-2026 according to the weekly report.
  • Earthworks man-hours have not changed for three weeks (74.0%), although cut rose by 6,000 m³ and fill by 4,000 m³ this week. Zones 1, 2 and 9 also report no earned man-hours this week, while 1,980 of the 3,594 man-hours earned this week (55%) came from procurement.
  • The quantities file and the Conclusion sheet still carry a second "fill" line (3,947,936 m³ total, 121,000 m³ done) whose done quantity equals the subgrade.
  • Tunnel 01 slab concrete is now 1,535 m³ against 1,402.72 m³ in the BOQ (109%). Tunnel 01 concrete is 5,590 m³ on the Major Quantities sheet but 4,055 m³ on the Major sheet, and box culvert concrete (6,274 m³) is measured against 10,940.61 m³ on the Major Quantities sheet but 3,870 m³ on the Major sheet (162%).
  • Quality: on the Quality-Stat sheet only the NCR line changed this week, and its inspection requests still show 490 issued but 1,687 closed and 236 pending. The MASTER LOG (refreshed 18-Nov-2026, after the data date) gives 78 quality NCRs (54 closed, 24 open) and 25 HSE NCRs against 80 (67 closed, 13 open), 1,982 shop drawings against 1,453, 103 MIRs against 113, 107 material submittals against 118, and 2,578 field inspection requests.
  • Safety: man-hours this week are 17,880 for the third week running. The sheet records 3 inductions and 9 toolbox talks this week, but the cumulative counts stay at 74 and 504, and year-to-date man-hours equal the cumulative total.
  • Invoices: the workbook lists 9 invoices, 86,818,263 SAR gross, none approved by the MODON PM and none paid; the presentation's financial chart still shows 70,621,360 SAR as paid. Invoice 9 carries a consultant approval date of 20-Nov-2026, after the data date. The invoice 10 backup is dated 17-Nov-2026 but covers the period to 30-Nov-2026, which has not ended. The contract value of 445,000,000 SAR is called "including VAT" on the Conclusion sheet but "excluding VAT" in the bill breakdown.
  • Activity counts differ: the Weekly Progress Report sheet gives 9,903 activities (2,452 completed, 940 in progress, 6,511 not started), the P6 update 8,625 (1,722, 602 and 6,301).
  • Issues: the Issues sheet still lists the SEC clash as active, while the issue log closed it on 30-Oct-2026. The presentation's target of 15-Nov-2026 for procurement has passed, and its look-ahead slide is still the August 2026 plan.
  • Procurement: the workbook's Proc. Stat summary now lists only GRP pipes and fittings (28,765 units) instead of all materials. The new material tracking sheet lists 662 purchase-order lines on 40 orders: 340 fully delivered, 92 partly and 230 not delivered. It counts order lines, not the BOQ quantities used in this report.
  • Street lighting is still 180 m, although the presentation shows street-lighting work on RD-A-1 and a photo shows the first poles being raised.
  • Several summary panels still show #REF! or #DIV/0! errors.
  • Photos: five are GPS-stamped 12–16 Nov 2026 and the approach-slab photo 16-Nov-2026. Not used: the riprap photo, stamped 18-Nov-2026 (after the data date), and the street-lighting pole photo (portrait, no stamp).
